front: A charge moving perpendicular to a uniform field travels in a circle of radius $r = {{c1::mv/(qB)}}$.
why: r = mv/(qB) is the core equation for charges in B fields and mass spec

front: A charged particle enters a field at an angle between $0$ and $90$ degrees. What path does it follow?
why: Helical path is a secondary case beyond the perpendicular circle

front: A magnetic field cannot change a particle's:
why: Magnetic force never changes kinetic energy: tested nearly every year

front: A molecule such as $O_2$ with unpaired electrons is {{c1::paramagnetic}} and is drawn into a magnetic field.
why: O2 paramagnetism from unpaired electrons is a frequent discrete

front: A proton moves east through a magnetic field pointing north. Which way is the magnetic force?
why: Right-hand-rule direction on a moving proton is a perennial discrete

front: A proton moves exactly parallel to a magnetic field. What magnetic force does it experience?
why: Zero force for motion parallel to B follows from F = qvB sin(theta)

front: A vertical wire carries current straight upward. You stand east of it. Which way does its magnetic field point at your position?
why: Right-hand rule for a wire field at a point is commonly asked

front: Ferromagnets stay magnetized after the external field is removed because their aligned {{c1::domains}} persist.
why: Ferromagnetic domains are prep-book detail, not outline

front: For a negative charge, the magnetic force points {{c1::opposite}} to the direction given by the right-hand rule.
why: Reversing the right-hand rule for negative charges is a perennial trap

front: Give the magnetic force on a moving charge.
why: F = qvB sin(theta) is the foundational magnetic force equation

front: How do paramagnetic and diamagnetic materials differ at the electron level?
why: Para vs diamagnetic electron-level distinction is commonly tested

front: How do you determine which end of a solenoid is its north pole?
why: Solenoid north-pole rule is a secondary right-hand-rule application

front: How does Earth's magnetic field compare in strength with a clinical MRI field?
why: Earth vs MRI field strength numbers are trivia

front: In a cyclotron, why is the orbital period of a charged particle independent of its speed?
why: Cyclotron period independence is a secondary derivation

front: Inside a long solenoid the field is $B = {{c1::\mu_0 nI}}$, uniform and directed along the axis.
why: Solenoid B = mu0 n I is prep-book detail, rarely calculated

front: Magnetic force is maximum when velocity and field are:
why: Max force when perpendicular follows from sin(theta); common discrete

front: The magnetic field inside a long straight wire's center is:
why: Field at the exact center of a wire is trivia

front: The strength of a wire's magnetic field varies with distance as:
why: B = mu0 I/(2 pi r) with 1/r falloff is the standard wire-field equation

front: What field does a straight current-carrying wire produce?
why: Circular field around a wire and right-hand rule are core

front: What path does a charge take entering a uniform $B$ field perpendicular?
why: Circular path for perpendicular entry is the foundational case

front: Why do magnetic field lines form closed loops?
why: No magnetic monopoles and closed field lines is a standard discrete

front: Why does deoxygenated blood change the MRI signal in functional imaging?
why: Deoxyhemoglobin paramagnetism links to BOLD; plausible passage step

front: Why does the magnetic force do no work?
why: Why magnetic force does no work; restates the no-KE-change card
